scSTAMP-seq (2025 preprint implementation)

scstamp-seq · bioRxiv version 1, posted 2025-10-02; DOI 10.1101/2025.10.01.679703. The later Nature Biotechnology publication is a distinct version and is not an extraction source for this attempt.

Scope: Describe the general source-defined assay from the stated starting specimen through the molecular readout and its decoding. Preserve source-described alternative assay implementations and their prerequisites without merging them into one execution. Include necessary preparation, controls, information attribution and delegated procedural dependencies; distinguish method construction from characterization experiments and biological applications.

How to read this view

Reading view of the supplied extraction. No fresh source review or experimental validation. Every Operation and Flow is retained. Recipes and evidence expand below each Operation. State labels are text previews; follow a label for the full record. Card order follows declared dependencies, with ID ties; it is not an execution schedule.

Workflow SHA-256: 32652da533c2d2ff2858d483bdad713314fd48787bda9e86c3e0b81d851dab69

Existing model/source review: supported. No new review performed.

  • Review omission · non-blocking

    The optional multi-PHO predictor already has the necessary measured-ratio and known-dose inputs. For future calibration transfer or reconstruction, it would be useful to document that the source demonstration used one outer-Cy5 PHO plus five unlabeled PHOs and whole-well DLP exposure with 10% tile overlap (primary p00031). These are design-specific execution details, not an omitted required transformation or a correction to an asserted fact.

    Action: advisory

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Resuspend and aliquot oligos under light protection; anneal equimolar PHO and CMO anchor, cool gradually and prepare working assemblies. Use the same strategy separately for optional MPO/anchor assemblies.
Information effect
Keeps PHO inner/outer and molecular-UMI identity; optional MPO identity is a sample label distinct from light exposure.
reagent
PHO: inner and outer 50 nt linked by a 360–380-nm-sensitive moiety; each half has 20-nt PCR handle, 4-nt domain barcode, random 6-nt UMI and 20-nt poly-A. Inner handle also binds CMO.
reagent
CMO anchor: 5′ cholesterol-TEG, 20-nt PHO-inner complement, 20-nt co-anchor complement, 3′ amino block. Co-anchor is added later, not in this anneal.
reagent
Optional MPO: no linker/outer half; 20-nt CMO/PCR handle, 4-nt multiplex discriminator, 6-nt MPO barcode, 6-nt UMI, 20-nt poly-A.
condition
Stocks: nuclease-free water AM9932, printed as “100 μm”; amber tubes 022363221, −20°C. Anneal recipe explicitly uses 100 μM: 2.4 μL PHO + 2.4 μL anchor + 7.2 μL duplex buffer 11-05-01-03, 20 μM intermediate. Bio-Rad thermal cycler, 94°C 3 min, cool 1°C/min to 4°C and hold; 500 nM working solution immediately before use, on ice or light-protected −20°C.
reagent
Reporter alternatives: inner-Cy3/outer-Cy5, selected outer-only Cy3/Cy5/FAM, or none; later experiments use outer-only or unlabeled designs.
reagent
Author-designed PHO/MPO/CMO oligos synthesized by IDT. CMO anchor/co-anchor design was adapted from Weber and MULTI-seq with DNA sequence changes; their distinct fatty-acid/labeling recipes or barcode lengths are not transferred.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
For the reported within-sample regional-normalization analysis, isolate bulk-HeLa gDNA at the delegated reference-preparation boundary.
Information effect
Creates a reference-material route independent of cell-indexed production libraries.
reagent
Dependency example isolates H9 gDNA with DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit 69504. The primary delegates HeLa isolation to this procedure but does not report the same H9 input mass as a HeLa quantity.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Maintain cultures, passage at the reported confluence, and seed on fibronectin-coated glass for labeling and optical access.
Information effect
Preserves cell identity and the intact spatial arrangement before dissociation.
reagent
High-glucose DMEM with GlutaMAX and sodium pyruvate (10569044), 10% FBS (catalogue printed as 10569044), 1% Pen-Strep (15140122).
condition
37°C, 5% CO2; passage 1:6 at 70–80% confluence with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA.
equipment
Treated flasks (156367) or 6-well plates (3516); imaging: fibronectin (5050)-coated glass-bottom 96-well plate P96–1.5H-N or 35-mm glass-coverslip dish P35G-1.5–20-C.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Strip chromatin using protease and GpC-methylate the reference DNA with M.CviPI/SAM before MspJI-seq processing.
Information effect
Measures potential site detection for normalization; it is not a single-cell accessibility measurement.
condition
Source-qualified dependency H9 example, not established HeLa amounts: 1.2 μg gDNA + 10 μL mix (100 μg protease, 1x GC buffer), 50°C 15 h/75°C 20 min/80°C 5 min; add 10 μL (8 U M.CviPI, 640 μM SAM, 1x GC buffer), 37°C 4 h; add 10 μL (4 U M.CviPI, 960 μM SAM), 37°C 4 h/65°C 20 min. Primary delegates the procedure but gives no HeLa mass.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Continue marked bulk DNA through the delegated scaled-up scMspJI-seq library boundary. Digestion, adapter construction and amplification internals of that unrepresented protocol are not invented.
Information effect
Creates sequencing material for the separate genomic detection-reference data.
condition
Dependency H9 example carries 100 ng marked DNA into scaled-up scMspJI-seq; this is not a reported HeLa mass. Deeper scaled-up recipe is unavailable in the packet.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Starting with the first labeled monolayer, repeat fresh unique PHO labeling, imaging, nested-mask illumination and washing; retain the joint cleavage code on cells. This alternative replaces the single-exposure implementation.
Information effect
Encodes region membership through the combination of PHO cleavage fractions. Current PHOs have no independent memory against subsequent illumination.
reagent
Fresh uniquely barcoded PHO/anchor labels for each round, prepared and embedded by the labeling procedure. Demonstration: PHO1 outer-Cy5, PHO2 outer-FAM, PHO3 outer-Cy3.
condition
Demonstrated design: 1000-μm fibronectin-patterned CYTOO 20-950-00 monolayer under 10x objective; three rounds, 30-s binary masks exposing 75%, 50%, 25% of area, with washes and pre/post imaging. These define the reported code, not mandatory settings for every assay.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Image labeled cells before illumination for reporter QC and, in the documented mCherry targeting design, collect tiled reporter images.
Information effect
Measures fluorescence while retaining labeled cells for illumination.
equipment
Nikon Ti-2, Yokogawa CSU-W1 SoRa, Andor iXon Life 888 EMCCD, 20x ELWD or 10x Plan Apo Lambda objective; FAM/Cy3/Cy5 lasers 488/561/640 nm at 100%.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Apply a user-defined DLP photomask/gradient, or uniform floodlight exposure for a cohort design; photolyze the PHO linker and retain the cell-associated barcode fraction.
Information effect
Physically encodes received light dose in the outer/inner molecule ratio; position remains an inference conditional on the illumination design.
equipment
Patterned route: Mightex Polygon400-G DMD, Excelitas X-Cite 360–380-nm UVA LED. Uniform alternative: 365-nm 50-W Everbeam B08635F9CX, acrylic diffuser and printed plate stand.
condition
Exposure intensity/duration belongs to the chosen design. Reported DLP saturation ~25–30 s and floodlight saturation ~10 min are characterization under their respective setups, not a universal dose. Reporter-targeting example: 30 s, 10% tile overlap.
condition
Route-specific feasibility demonstrations used uniform floodlight: droplet capture used outer-Cy5-PHO-labeled HeLa cells at 0, 1 or 10 min; scSTAMP-MAT used outer-Cy5-PHO-labeled HeLa/U2OS cells in separate wells with no light or 1 min. These are demonstrated dose-cohort designs, not universal durations for patterned encoding. The authors describe broader patterned-light/modular architectures; these demonstrations do not establish every optical-design/capture-route combination.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Dissociate, quench trypsin with serum-containing medium, wash, resuspend and strain; keep the retained single-cell suspension on ice.
Information effect
Physical spatial arrangement is lost on dissociation; membrane label identities retain optical attribution for downstream decoding.
reagent
0.25% trypsin-EDTA; serum-containing DMEM; 1 mL cold 1x DPBS−/− without calcium/magnesium (source prints 14040133).
equipment
35-μm nylon mesh into 5-mL round-bottom polystyrene tube (352235), kept on ice.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Acquire post-exposure fluorescence and process images for cleavage QC. Reporter-bearing encoded material is inspected while remaining available for collection.
Information effect
Observes cleavage. No production feedback, sorting gate or loading adjustment is inferred from fluorescence QC alone.
equipment
Same microscopy setup and excitation alternatives as pre-imaging.
software
Nikon nd2 → ImageJ/FIJI TIFF; custom MATLAB R2022a and Python 3.9.0.
condition
Optional characterization choices: initial three z-planes spaced 15 μm, maximum-intensity projection; later one plane/outer-only fluorescence. Gradient QC removes saturated pixels, subtracts background, normalizes channel stacks and uses Cy5/Cy3 over 23 s. Coculture segmentation uses Cellpose2.0 cyto2 on pre-cleavage outer-Cy5 and per-cell mean intensity (69 frames). These measurements are supporting observations.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
For the droplet alternative, generate GEMs, lyse copartitioned cells and copy endogenous polyadenylated RNA and PHO DNA with bead oligos; include the source-described template-switch extension.
Information effect
Introduces 10X cell barcode and capture UMI independently of PHO-intrinsic domain and oligo UMIs.
equipment
Chromium Controller, Next GEM Single Cell 3′ LT v3.1 kit 1000325. Registered guide is CG000399 Rev B; primary revision is unspecified.
reagent
Guide bead primer contains TruSeq-R1/16-nt 10X barcode/12-nt UMI/30-nt poly(dT). Supplement describes PHO copying and TSO extension; custom spatial primers are added at the later amplification boundary.
condition
Guide GEM-RT: 53°C 45 min, 85°C 5 min, 4°C hold. Guide starting recommendations: ~1667 cells loaded/~500 recovered, optimal 100–600 cells/μL; these are not reported scSTAMP execution values.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Use the source-described MAT plate-capture/lysis boundary before simultaneous RNA/PHO copying and chromatin marking.
Information effect
Preserves per-cell compartmental identity; molecular RNA/PHO and genomic-origin tags are introduced in subsequent operations.
equipment
384-well plates, FACS, 12-channel pipette for oil and Nanodrop II for downstream dispensing, as specified in the delegated scMAT source.
reagent
Delegated scMAT per well: 4 μL Vapor-Lock; 100 nL 7.5 ng/μL barcoded RT primer; 100 nL lysis mix (0.175% IGEPAL, 1.75 mM dNTP, 1:1,250,000 ERCC 4456740, 0.19 U RNase inhibitor). Dependency has 4-nt UMI; frozen-primary MAT length remains unspecified, so no 4/6-nt transfer is asserted.
condition
Delegated scMAT after sorting: unless cryopreserved, heat 65°C 3 min and return to ice.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Preload barcoded primer and lysis buffer under Vapor-Lock, FACS one cell per well, heat and return to ice.
Information effect
Establishes a cell-specific reaction compartment and introduced ERCC reference; the capture barcode becomes molecular during copying.
equipment
384-well plate HSP3801, FACS; manual 12-channel oil dispensing, Nanodrop II downstream liquid handling.
reagent
Per well: 4 μL Vapor-Lock 981611; 100 nL uniquely barcoded RT primer 7.5 ng/μL with 6-nt UMI; 100 nL lysis mix: 0.175% IGEPAL CA-630, 1.75 mM dNTPs, 1:1,250,000 ERCC mix 4456740, 0.19 U RNase inhibitor 2313A. Primer architecture: poly-T, cell barcode, UMI, 5′ Illumina adapter and T7 promoter; exact nucleotide sequence not recovered.
condition
After sorting: 65°C 3 min, return to ice.
condition
Primary describes fluorophore-assisted enrichment of cells at spatial locations by cell sorting as a possible use; it supplies no specific enrichment gate. This is optional on reporter-bearing designs and is not asserted for every FACS capture.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Break GEMs, recover pooled aqueous material without aspirating it during oil removal, and purify first strands on silane beads with ethanol washing and elution.
Information effect
Removes physical GEM compartments while preserving molecular cell-barcode attribution.
reagent
Guide: discard 125 μL Recovery Agent/Partitioning Oil without aspirating aqueous sample; add 200 μL Dynabeads cleanup mix, RT 10 min; wash pellet 300 then 200 μL 80% ethanol, elute 35.5 μL Elution Solution I and transfer 35 μL. Manufacturer details are qualified by the primary’s unnamed guide revision.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Simultaneously reverse-transcribe RNA/copy PHO DNA and methylate accessible GpC cytosines with M.CviPI/SAM at the initial lysate state; then synthesize second-strand DNA.
Information effect
Encodes chromatin accessibility as introduced GpC methylation, distinct from endogenous 5mC; gives RNA/PHO molecules a shared cell-and-origin capture identity before genomic adapter ligation.
reagent
Optimized delegated scMAT mix: 150 nL, 0.7 U RNaseOUT, 1.17x first-strand buffer, 11.67 mM DTT, 3.5 U SuperScript II, 0.19 mM SAM, 1.17x GC buffer, 0.1 U M.CviPI M0227S; 37°C 1 h/4°C 5 min/65°C 10 min/70°C 10 min. These replace the RNA-only 42°C RT conditions on this route.
reagent
Then 1.75 μL second-strand mix: 1.74x buffer, 0.35 mM dNTP, 0.14 U E. coli ligase, 0.56 U polymerase I, 0.03 U RNase H; 16°C 2 h. Dependency’s separate buffer-optimization experiments are not added to this recipe.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Reverse-transcribe mRNA/ERCC and copy polyadenylated PHO/MPO DNA with the well-specific capture primer, then synthesize second strands.
Information effect
Introduces shared cell attribution, capture UMI, RA5/5′ Illumina and T7 interfaces; retains PHO domain/UMI and optional MPO identity.
reagent
Per well add 150 nL RT mix: 0.7 U RNaseOUT, 2.34x first-strand buffer, 23.34 mM DTT, 3.5 U SuperScript II; 42°C 75 min, 4°C 5 min, 70°C 10 min, 4°C hold.
reagent
Add 1.75 μL second-strand mix: 1.74x second-strand buffer, 0.35 mM dNTP, 0.14 U E. coli ligase, 0.56 U E. coli polymerase I, 0.03 U RNase H; 16°C 2 h then 4°C hold.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Represent the source-supported custom amplification/fractionation unit through its two retained fractions. Primary Methods places custom-primer amplification before a 0.6x split; Supplementary Fig.10 places separation before cDNA amplification. Preserve both statements without reconciling stage equivalence or asserting a single exact internal handoff. For the frozen general-assay scope, this unit asserts the qualified input, two retained fractions and their distinct library continuations; exact internal order and adapter-transfer identity remain detail limits.
Information effect
Retains distinct endogenous and barcode fractions linked by 10X cell attribution; no equivalence between the differing amplification-stage descriptions is inferred.
reagent
Primary custom mix: inner and outer PHO primers at a working 2.5 μM; 50 μL 10X amplification master mix + 15 μL 10X cDNA primer mix + 1 μL scSTAMP 10X primer mix. Do not add the guide’s separate unmodified 65-μL mix to this recipe.
condition
Primary Methods: amplify then 0.6x AMPure XP, 30 min; subsequent plate-strategy invocation leaves exact additional/adjusted ratios unassigned. Supplement instead says separation prior to cDNA amplification. This unit deliberately leaves that exact internal order unresolved.
condition
Guide amplification program at the delegated boundary: 98°C 3 min; repeated 98°C 15 s/63°C 20 s/72°C 1 min; 72°C 1 min final, 4°C hold. Guide optimization starting points are 13 cycles for <500 targeted recovered cells and 12 for 500–1000. Primary-selected cycle count is not reported.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Strip chromatin with protease, glucosylate 5hmC with T4-BGT/UDP-glucose, apply the second protease treatment, then digest methylcytosine-containing gDNA with MspJI to create double-strand breaks.
Information effect
Protects 5hmC from downstream detection and converts introduced/endogenous methylcytosine information into genomic fragments; RNA/PHO cell tags remain separate.
reagent
Delegated scMAT: 400 nL protease mix (6 μg protease 19155, 6.25x NEBuffer4), 50°C 15 h/75°C 20 min/80°C 5 min; then 500 nL 5hmC block (1 U T4-BGT M0357L, 6x UDP-glucose, 1x NEBuffer4), 37°C 16 h; then 500 nL protease mix (2 μg, 1x NEBuffer4), 50°C 3 h/75°C 20 min/80°C 5 min.
reagent
500 nL MspJI mix: 1x NEBuffer4, 8x activator, 0.1 U MspJI R0661L; 37°C 4.5 h then 65°C 25 min.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Continue the retained endogenous fraction using the 10X cleanup wash/elution boundary. Do not add a second 0.6x split or discard the retained spatial fraction by importing the unmodified guide literally.
Information effect
Keeps endogenous cell-barcoded cDNA apart from the spatial-library branch.
reagent
Guide continuation: two 200-μL 80% ethanol pellet washes, 40.5 μL Buffer EB, recover 40 μL. This is the post-partition endogenous fraction; the primary custom 30-min split overrides the guide’s standalone 5-min 0.6x cleanup timing.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Ligate cell/gDNA-origin-tagged double-stranded adapters to genomic breaks. Only after both molecular origins carry cell identity, pool distinct-barcode wells and discard oil.
Information effect
Adds genomic cell/origin/UMI/T7 identity separate from RNA/PHO capture tags, enabling later cell-level linkage after pooling.
reagent
Delegated scMAT: 320 nL 125 nM uniquely barcoded ds adapters (sequence delegated to Sen et al.); 680 nL ligation mix (1.47x T4 ligase buffer, 5.88 mM ATP, 140 U T4 DNA ligase), 16°C 16 h. No exact adapter nucleotide sequence or fragment-end structure is supplied.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Perform the first SPRI partition; transfer short spatial-product supernatant and retain endogenous cDNA on beads for its separate route.
Information effect
Separates molecular sizes while retaining the common cell attribution needed to reconnect readouts.
reagent
0.7x AMPure XP A63881; room temperature 15 min, magnet 5 min. Keep both the endogenous beads and transferred spatial supernatant.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
At the first scMAT cleanup boundary, use the primary’s plate spatial-fractionation strategy and retain both the short spatial fraction and the barcoded endogenous RNA/gDNA fraction. Do not concatenate the unmodified scMAT 1x cleanup as an additional partition.
Information effect
Preserves both molecular origins and their shared cell linkage; spatial tags enter their separate PCR route.
reagent
Primary invokes the plate partition/recovery strategy: initial 0.7x AMPure XP, room temperature 15 min/magnet 5 min; spatial supernatant proceeds to high-SPRI/isopropanol recovery. The older scMAT 1x AMPure cleanup/30-min incubation/30-μL elution/6.4-μL concentrate describes the unadapted dependency boundary and is not appended to the primary partition.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Run the analytical aliquot on Bioanalyzer HS; determine cDNA concentration over the guide-defined size range and calculate total/carry-forward yield with dilution correction.
Information effect
Produces the yield estimate used by the guide’s sample-index PCR cycle rule.
equipment
Agilent Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity chip and 2100 Expert Software. Run 1 μL at 1:10 dilution, or undiluted for low-RNA cells; quantify ~200–9000 bp, multiply pg/μL concentration by recovered 40 μL and dilution factor, divide by 1000 for ng.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Process the production aliquot through the manufacturer’s fragmentation/end-repair/A-tail unit and double-sided selection; retain the second bead-selected fragment fraction.
Information effect
Changes endogenous cDNA length and ends while retaining cell barcode and UMI interfaces on the selected library fragments.
reagent
Guide: 10 μL cDNA + 25 μL Buffer EB + 15 μL fragmentation mix; 32°C 5 min fragmentation, 65°C 30 min end repair/A-tailing, 4°C hold. Then 0.6x/0.8x SPRIselect (30 μL then 10 μL); first keep supernatant, second keep beads; two 125-μL 80% ethanol washes, elute 50.5 μL Buffer EB, recover 50 μL.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Amplify the retained T7-bearing RNA/gDNA-derived endogenous products by IVT at the delegated boundary.
Information effect
Retains molecular-origin and cell associations for downstream analytical separation.
condition

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Convert IVT-amplified endogenous material to its Illumina library following the explicitly delegated scMAT/scAba/scMspJI procedures at the supported input/output boundary.
Information effect
Retains the association needed to join transcript counts and PHO counts from each captured cell.
condition
Internal post-IVT recipe and exact final adapters are delegated to Chialastri/scMAT and its scAba-seq/scMspJI-seq references; the underlying recipes are not packet sources. CEL-Seq2 random-hexamer RT and its sequencing cycles are not substituted.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Bind the spatial barcode fraction with high SPRI/isopropanol conditions, retain washed bead-bound products, elute and concentrate. The plate recipe is explicit and MAT invokes it; the droplet invocation is preserved at its supported recovery boundary without inventing cumulative 0.6x/0.7x ratios.
Information effect
Retains cell, domain and oligo-molecule identities while removing unretained soluble material.
reagent
Plate/MAT-delegated recipe: add 2.5x SPRI beads and 1.8x 100% isopropanol relative to original pre-cleanup volume (plate total beads 3.2x); room temperature 15 min, magnet 5 min, discard supernatant, two 80% ethanol washes, elute 30 μL water, concentrate to 15 μL in Vacufuge plus. Droplet primary reports its own 0.6x split and invokes this strategy without specifying exact ratio replacement/addition; no cumulative recipe is asserted.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Use one selected, nonoverlapping dual-index set, amplify by the manufacturer’s input-yield cycle rule, and double-sided-select the final endogenous library.
Information effect
Adds selected i5/i7 sample indexes and final P5/P7 sequencing construct; preserves cell barcode/UMI for endogenous counts.
reagent
Guide: 30 μL sample + 50 μL Amp Mix 2000103 + 20 μL one Dual Index TT Set A (PN-3000431); record well ID, avoid overlapping indexes. Primary selected well/index is unspecified.
condition
Guide index PCR: 98°C 45 s; repeat 98°C 20 s/54°C 30 s/72°C 20 s; final 72°C 1 min, 4°C hold. Carry-forward input: 0.25–25 ng →14–16 cycles; 25–150 ng →12–14; 150–500 ng →10–12. This is a manufacturer control rule, not an observed primary cycle choice.
reagent
Guide final selection: 0.6x then 0.8x SPRIselect (60 then 20 μL), first retain supernatant then beads; two 200-μL 80% ethanol washes, elute 35.5 μL Buffer EB and transfer 35 μL.
reagent
Manufacturer endogenous-library reference sense construct, not the PHO library: 5’-AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACAC-N10 -ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT-N16-N12-TTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTVN- cDNA_Insert-AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC-N10-ATCTCGTATGCCGTCTTCTGCTTG-3’. N10 are sample indexes, N16 cell barcode and N12 UMI; selected bases remain unspecified.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Anneal biotinylated poly-A primer to the allocated aRNA and bind RNase-free streptavidin beads; discard supernatant, wash and retain the enriched bead suspension.
Information effect
Enriches transcript-derived molecules; the independently reserved unenriched portion supplies epigenomic detection.
reagent
Delegated scMAT: 6 μL aRNA + 2 μL 1 μM IDT standard-desalted 5′-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA/3BioTEG/-3′, room temperature 10 min. RNase-free Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 65001 in 8 μL 2x B&W, room temperature 15 min/300 rpm; discard supernatant, wash twice 1x B&W, resuspend beads in 10 μL nuclease-free water.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Continue the separately retained unenriched endogenous preparation into the delegated genomic Illumina library; do not use discarded RNA-enrichment supernatant by assumption.
Information effect
Carries introduced and endogenous methylcytosine information with cell and genomic-origin identity into sequencing.
condition
Internal post-IVT genomic-library recipe and exact adapter sequences remain delegated to scAba-seq/scMspJI-seq and Sen et al.; no specific uninspected fragmentation or end geometry is asserted.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Use the delegated alternatives: on-bead RT, or heat elution and transfer of enriched RNA followed by RT; construct the final Illumina transcriptome library at the delegated boundary.
Information effect
Retains transcript/cell attribution while producing a distinct endogenous transcriptome library.
condition
Alternatives in scMAT: on-bead processing into RT, or 70°C 2 min then rapid magnet separation and transfer of supernatant. Use 5 μL enriched product for RT in either case; subsequent library recipe delegated to scAba-seq/scMspJI-seq. No selected option is claimed.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Amplify the treated aliquot with sample-index primer, perform the second ExoSAP treatment, double-sided selection and ethanol washes, and retain the final indexed eluate.
Information effect
Adds selected sample index/P7 interface while preserving per-cell PHO and optional MPO identity.
reagent
Plate recipe: 7 μL treated aliquot, 22.5 μL 2x PCR mix, 2 μL each 10 μM RPI and sample-index primer, water to 45 μL; 6–12 cycles 94°C 10 s/60°C 30 s/72°C 30 s. Add 5 μL ExoSAP-IT to 45 μL PCR, 37°C 15 min. Purify 1.2x double-sided (0.90x left/0.30x right), wash twice 80% ethanol, elute 20 μL water. Route-specific adapter identities follow the supplementary schematics; no selected index nucleotide is invented.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Decode cell/genomic-origin attribution and call genomic methylcytosine positions at the delegated scMAT boundary; apply its explicit preceding-base rule to separate accessibility from endogenous methylation and then subtype endogenous contexts.
Information effect
Infers introduced versus endogenous mark origin through the stated sequence-context exclusions; retains cell linkage to RNA/PHO. Exact lower-level mapping and sequence matching remain delegated.
software
Custom Perl 5mC caller/preceding-base context rule in the represented scMAT dependency; underlying mapping/calling internals delegated to Sen et al. with adjustments.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Sequence the selected plate-RNA, droplet-RNA or MAT-RNA endogenous library as distinct invocations; preserve its route/sample/cell identity in the read data.
Information effect
Converts endogenous library molecules into read data with retained sample/cell and molecule-of-origin identity.
equipment
Reported primary alternatives: HiSeq 4000 or NextSeq 500.
condition
Manufacturer endogenous 10X recommendations: paired-end dual index, ≥20,000 pairs/cell; R1/i7/i5/R2 = 28/10/10/90 cycles. These are guide recommendations, not reported primary run lengths and not spatial-library settings.
condition
Delegated scMAT transcriptome recommendation: minimum R1 25 bp and R2 50 bp; not an actual frozen-primary run specification.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Sequence the indexed spatial DNA library on a reported Illumina platform to produce paired reads for the spatial decoder.
Information effect
Converts the material barcode carrier into observed sequence data; spatial position is not read directly.
equipment
Illumina HiSeq 4000 or NextSeq 500. The frozen primary does not give actual spatial read-cycle counts.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
For reported cross-dataset comparisons, normalize to CPM and plot a 75-bp moving average; for differing regions within a sample additionally use the bulk detected-site reference. When comparing to HeLa DNase sites, retain their score groups.
Information effect
Relates sample signal to external genomic annotations or independent detection references; neither reference is mixed with sample material.
condition
Cross-dataset counts per million and 75-bp moving average; within-sample regions further normalized by detected bulk-HeLa methylcytosines after chromatin stripping/GpC marking. External HeLa DNase-I sites grouped by detection score.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Assign read1 cell barcode/capture UMI; read2 domain-specific primer, spatial barcode and oligo UMI. Distinguish optional MPOs by the extra read2 multiplex identifier; count joint-UMI combinations.
Information effect
Decodes molecular identities into counts without conflating capture UMI with oligo UMI or sample multiplex identity with position.
software
Custom Perl scripts on Linux HPC; exact match/error-correction settings and frozen code revision remain unreported in the packet.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Map read2 sense-strand to hg19 RefSeq plus ERCCs, distribute multimappers evenly, consolidate gene isoforms, deduplicate UMIs and remove globally undetected genes.
Information effect
Converts endogenous read identities into cell-resolved transcript counts while retaining introduced ERCC reference counts.
software
BWA 0.7.15-r1140; sense read2 alignment to hg19 RefSeq +92 ERCCs; uniform multimapper distribution, gene-level isoform consolidation and UMI deduplication.
condition
Remove genes undetected in every cell.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Apply the route-specific cell filters, log-normalize counts, obtain variable-gene PCs and use the elbow criterion for PC selection, then cluster/UMAP and assign cell groups using expression markers and, where stated, barcode counts.
Information effect
Makes explicit analytical selection and clustering decisions; ERCC is a plate-lysis input/reference, not a PHO-dose calibrant.
condition
Reported plate rule: >1000 genes, >1000 unique transcripts, <20% ERCC; droplet: >200 genes, >200 unique transcripts, <5% mitochondrial counts. These are analysis criteria, not molecular admission or universal preparation rules.
software
Seurat 4.3.0, R 4.2.2, RStudio 2022.12.0+353; default NormalizeData, top 2000 variable genes, elbow-selected PCs, FindNeighbors/FindClusters/RunUMAP.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Quantify accessibility/methylation in 5-kb bins and binarize; form pseudobulk profiles using transcriptome-derived cell groups. Preserve the reported conditional comparison/clustering choices without making them universal.
Information effect
Aggregates sites while preserving cell identity and distinguishing accessibility from endogenous methylation.
condition
5-kb bins → binary scores; pseudobulk by transcriptome cell type. HeLa/U2OS comparison: top 2% most-variable bins, remove low-variance bins, PCA, compare clusters to RNA cell types. Minimum 15,000 applies to Supplementary Fig.14a,b with threshold variable unspecified; no invented universal count filter.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
For simultaneous multiple-PHO noise reduction, group measured ratios by known dose, derive effective regions and extend nearest regions equally over uncovered intervals.
Information effect
Produces a calibration/reference data dependency, not feedback governing physical UV exposure.
condition
Effective-region thresholds 10% and 90%; overlapping regions are ambiguous; extend nearest two equally across uncovered gaps. Demonstration used six simultaneous PHOs and five doses, not compulsory numbers for the general assay.

      "rationale": "Association: Cellwise cleavage fractions support the position/exposure inference."

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Relate measured PHO cleavage ratios to the imposed light pattern; for the sequential nested-mask implementation use the joint PHO code to assign its designed region. Retain ambiguity rather than invent a general numerical dose-to-coordinate inverse.
Information effect
Infers spatial membership from a molecular light-dose signal and its design; actual calibration/inverse and ambiguous cases remain qualified.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Compare each PHO ratio to all effective dose regions, allow overlapping matches, sum votes across PHOs and assign the highest-vote illumination level.
Information effect
Infers an illumination level using a documented reference rule; does not establish exact reproduction of published assignment accuracy.

Combines independently read molecular origins without inventing barcode sequences, mappings, general spatial inverses or historical sample identities.

Declared gaps and limitations

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:G01

    Exact scSTAMP PHO/MPO/CMO, domain-handle, plate RT, inner/outer PCR, sample-index and custom 10X PHO-primer sequences/modification positions cannot be recovered from the inspected packet renditions. Primary p00021 points to Supplementary Table 1; p00022 and HTML p00170 contain only its title; the inspected supplementary PDF rendition contains figure captions rather than that table. Domain architecture and operation-specific primer roles are supported, so this is a nonblocking sequence/recipe limit for the declared general assay, not permission to invent identities or substitute dependency oligos.

    Next evidence: Recover/register Supplementary Table 1 from the same 2025-10-02 preprint version, with full sequences, modifications, named alternatives and their role assignments; inspect any table image or spreadsheet and preserve selected identities. No later publication should substitute.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:G02

    The primary delegates endogenous plate and multiomic Illumina-library construction to scMAT (primary p00043/p00045). Registered scMAT p00045/p00051 further delegate IVT/post-IVT conversion to scAba-seq/scMspJI-seq protocols 6,7, which are not registered packet sources. T7-IVT, enrichment, RT and final Illumina-library boundaries are supported, but their full internal recipe and genomic adapter details are not. Nonblocking for a qualified general architecture with declared delegation; no executable complete library recipe or specific uninspected fragmentation/adapter mechanism is asserted.

    Next evidence: Register the exact scAba-seq and scMspJI-seq library-preparation protocols (references 6 and 7 in the registered Chialastri scMAT preprint), including T7 IVT, aRNA handling, conversion, adapter/UMI design and final amplification; establish which subprocedures the frozen primary inherits.

  • Non-blocking · droplet_timing_detail

    Primary droplet Methods p00044 place amplification before the 0.6x PHO/endogenous split, whereas Supplementary Figure 10 continuation p00019 places the split before amplification. Both refer to the adapted droplet library; MULTI-seq p00228 reports after-amplification separation but cannot establish the intended scSTAMP order. The exact timing remains unknown. This is nonblocking for the frozen general-assay scope: droplet_amp_partition preserves both descriptions at a qualified composite boundary, and the primary identifies the retained spatial and endogenous fractions and their respective Illumina-library continuations. An unqualified single exact timing/interface claim would remain unsupported; no stage equivalence or reconciled execution is asserted.

    Next evidence: A frozen-version detailed droplet protocol, author correction or sufficiently explicit original Supplementary Figure 10 annotation establishing whether the PHO/endogenous split is before or after the custom cDNA amplification, and what each separated fraction subsequently receives.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:G04

    Primary p00044 reports a 0.6x droplet split and refers to the plate small-molecule strategy; p00043 uses 0.7x then additional 2.5x beads with 1.8x isopropanol. The packet text does not specify whether the plate first partition replaces, follows, or merely exemplifies the droplet split, or the exact adjusted ratios. Fraction identities and downstream routes are supported, so this is a nonblocking quantitative recipe-transfer limit. Do not assert a cumulative 0.6x+0.7x+2.5x bead recipe.

    Next evidence: Same-version droplet size-selection instructions specifying the retained fraction at each addition, reference volume for ratios, and whether the 0.7x plate partition is omitted when 0.6x has already separated endogenous cDNA.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:G05

    Exact scSTAMP-MAT capture-primer UMI length/sequence remains unassigned: primary p00013 gives a UMI without a length, primary plate-only p00041 specifies six bases, and delegated scMAT p00045 specifies four bases. These have different procedure applicability, so they are not established contradictory execution claims. Nonblocking while the MAT interface retains cell/mRNA-PHO attribution and an unspecified UMI; it blocks asserting one precise MAT primer by silently selecting either source.

    Next evidence: The frozen primary Supplementary Table 1 or an explicit scSTAMP-MAT protocol statement assigning its RT primer sequence and UMI length, separately from the plate-only RNA and 2022 scMAT implementations.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:G06

    Supplementary Figure 12 p00021 describes enrichment separating mRNA/gDNA-derived products, while delegated scMAT p00047 explicitly sequences RNA-enriched material for transcripts and unenriched material for methylated cytosines. The protocol supports retention of enriched and unenriched analytical portions but does not specify the physical split volume or conclusively map gDNA sequencing to an enrichment flowthrough. Nonblocking with the unenriched prerequisite and inferred split retained; unsupported flowthrough routing must not be asserted.

    Next evidence: Frozen-version instructions or annotated Supplementary Figure 12 showing when/how IVT product is allocated to unenriched epigenomic and enriched transcriptomic libraries, the retained fractions, and any use of enrichment flowthrough.

  • Non-blocking · information:G01

    Exact nucleotide identities remain unavailable in inspected packet passages: primary p00021 refers PHO/MPO/CMO sequences to Supplementary Table 1, p00022 and HTML p00170 contain only its label, and the supplied supplement contains figure descriptions rather than that table. This leaves PHO IDs, anchor sequences and custom plate/10X primer sequences unspecified; do not substitute the MULTI-seq additive primer. Primary plate capture explicitly has a 6-nt UMI (p00041), while the represented older Grün and scMAT dependencies describe 4-nt capture UMIs; that difference is not by itself a contradiction of the primary plate route and does not establish the selected scSTAMP-MAT capture-primer length. Nonblocking for source-qualified assay architecture, but prevents an exact sequence-level decoding or executable primer specification.

    Next evidence: Frozen preprint v1 Supplementary Table 1 with complete PHO/MPO/CMO and plate/10X amplification oligos; identify the RNA/PHO capture primer and matched genomic-adapter barcode mapping used for the scSTAMP-MAT variant.

  • Non-blocking · droplet_handoff_detail

    The precise droplet amplification/separation handoff is unresolved: primary Methods p00044 specifies custom-primer cDNA amplification followed by 0.6x SPRI, whereas Supplementary Fig.10 text p00019 says PHO-derived molecules are separated prior to cDNA amplification. The adapted MULTI-seq dependency p00228 describes separation following amplification, but its v2/additive-primer workflow does not prove equivalence to every amplification stage in the scSTAMP schematic. The meanings of those stages and the exact adapter-transfer handoff remain unknown. This is nonblocking for the frozen general-assay scope because the represented composite retains both wordings and the primary establishes the capture-to-spatial-and-endogenous-library boundary. A single reconciled, unqualified timing/adapter-transfer claim remains unsupported until the stage meanings are established.

    Next evidence: A frozen v1 protocol clarification or detailed annotated Supplementary Fig.10 specifying which amplification each statement denotes, when custom inner/outer primers act, and which material enters the 0.6x selection. The full diagram can clarify context, but any new supporting text must be registered as packet evidence.

  • Non-blocking · information:G03

    Primary p00048 supplies read roles and joint-UMI counting, p00018/p00008 supply ratio-based inference, and p00049 supplies the optional known-dose voting rule. The inspected Methods do not specify exact normalized-ratio scaling, zero-inner handling, sequence-match/error-correction rules or a general numerical dose-to-coordinate inverse. These are nonblocking limits for a qualified source-described decoding architecture, but prevent claiming exact reproduction of numerical assignments or universally unique coordinates from any illumination pattern.

    Next evidence: The frozen-version custom Perl scripts and documentation named in primary p00058, including PHO primer/barcode matching, count normalization, zero-count handling and the illumination-design-to-position association. No code revision is supplied in the inspected packet.

  • Non-blocking · information:G04

    The represented scMAT preprint delegates post-cleanup/IVT and final library preparation to scAba-seq/scMspJI-seq (p00045,p00051), and genomic adapter design to Sen et al. These underlying protocol recipes and exact adapter sequences are not represented as separate packet sources. Primary p00007 and Supplementary Fig.12 independently establish IVT, RNA enrichment and final library endpoints, so absent internals are nonblocking architecture-detail gaps; they do not authorize inventing IVT conditions, fragmentation or adapter sequence identities. CEL-Seq2 is a distinct cited dependency, not sufficient evidence for transferring all its steps/settings.

    Next evidence: The scAba-seq and scMspJI-seq protocol sections specifically delegated by Chialastri scMAT Methods, including T7 IVT and subsequent Illumina library construction, plus the Sen et al. genomic adapter specification and cell/origin barcode correspondence.

  • Non-blocking · information:G05

    Supplementary Fig.12 describes endogenous IVT followed by RNA enrichment and transcriptomic/epigenomic library outputs. The scMAT dependency explicitly uses RNA-enriched material for RNA and unenriched material for methylcytosines (p00047), while its enrichment procedure discards supernatant (p00049). It does not state the exact reservation or division of the common IVT product across these preparations. Preserve separate enriched-RNA and unenriched epigenomic preparations at the supported delegated boundary; do not assert the discarded enrichment supernatant becomes the epigenomic library. Nonblocking for those qualified boundaries; a fully explicit aliquot graph would require the missing allocation.

    Next evidence: The frozen scSTAMP-MAT/scMAT preparation map showing which IVT volume is reserved unenriched for epigenomic sequencing, which aliquot undergoes RNA enrichment, and which on-bead versus heat-elution option is selected, if an executed version is claimed.

  • Non-blocking · information:G06

    Primary p00053 states a minimum of 15,000 for Supplementary Fig.14a,b but does not identify the threshold variable or associate it separately with accessibility versus endogenous methylation. The supplement p00023 labels panels as unique-site counts versus sequencing depth, which does not uniquely resolve the threshold. Nonblocking for general endpoint and binning/clustering architecture; retain the stated threshold with its unassigned variable rather than imposing an invented universal QC rule.

    Next evidence: Frozen preprint v1 analysis documentation or code explicitly naming the quantity tested against 15,000 and the panel-specific filtering rule.

  • Non-blocking · genomic_calling_detail

    The primary invokes scMAT genomic analysis; represented scMAT gives the context assignment rule but delegates its underlying genomic mapping/site-calling pipeline to Sen et al. Exact genomic barcode matching, UMI handling and site-calling internals are not reconstructed. The supported read-to-cell/site/context boundary is represented; no exact numerical reproduction is claimed.

    Next evidence: The frozen scMAT supplementary software/Sen et al. scMspJI-seq analysis protocol specifying genomic read layout, adapter barcode matching and methylcytosine site calling.

  • Non-blocking · primary_read_cycles

    The inspected primary reports HiSeq4000/NextSeq500 sequencing and read roles without actual cycle counts. Manufacturer 28/10/10/90 and scMAT minimum lengths remain separately attributed recommendations; no primary run configuration is inferred.

    Next evidence: Same-version sequencing methods or run-design documentation assigning spatial and endogenous read lengths to each implementation.

oligo_reagents · material

Author-designed IDT PHOs and CMO anchor reagents, with optional MPOs. Each PHO retains covalently linked inner/outer 50-nt DNA domains, domain identity, a random 6-nt UMI per domain and poly-A capture tails. Select one reporter scheme: inner-Cy3/outer-Cy5, outer-only Cy3/Cy5/FAM, or no reporter. These are choices, not cumulative labels. Exact oligos are unavailable in the packet table rendition.

spatial_transcriptome_multiome · data

Declared endpoint: cell-linked transcriptome and qualified optical exposure/region attribution; for the MAT alternative, linked DNA accessibility and endogenous methylation profiles. Optional known-dose vote predictions can accompany attribution. The demonstrated droplet (0/1/10-min) and MAT (no-light/1-min) floodlight designs supply exposure-cohort attribution, not within-well position; the broader patterned-light/capture combinations are source-described architecture rather than all experimentally demonstrated combinations. This is not reproduction of any historical numeric dataset.

Modules: optional navigation groups
Live specimen and oligo preparation · Module prep

Prepares the intact specimen and membrane-carried information substrates before optical encoding.

  • culture · Maintain and seed live cells
  • assemble · Prepare and anneal labeling oligos
  • label · Embed labels in live membranes
Alternative optical encoding and optional inspection · Module optics

Groups light-pattern encoding and its optional reporter observations/targeting; single versus sequential implementations remain explicit.

  • image_before · Acquire optional pre-illumination images
  • target_masks · Generate optional reporter-guided masks
  • encode_single · Photocleave labels with selected exposure design
  • encode_sequential · Encode optional sequential combinations
  • image_after · Inspect optional post-illumination cleavage
Single-cell collection · Module collection

Dissociation removes spatial arrangement and exposes the alternative single-cell capture interfaces.

  • collect · Collect optically encoded single cells
Plate transcriptome capture and partition · Module plate

Cell identity is introduced in wells before pooling; partition exposes independently retained spatial and endogenous fractions.

  • plate_capture · Sort and lyse individual cells for RNA profiling
  • plate_copy · Copy RNA and oligo tags and synthesize second strands
  • plate_pooling · Pool cell-tagged products
  • plate_partition · Partition short spatial products from endogenous cDNA
Spatial-library construction · Module spatial_library_module

Joins only the explicitly invoked spatial continuations while retaining route-specific capture/adapter identity, the sampled PCR aliquot and QC data.

  • spatial_enrichment · Recover the short spatial DNA fraction
  • spatial_PCR1_op · Amplify and extend spatial barcode products
  • spatial_aliquot · Withdraw and treat the spatial-PCR aliquot
  • spatial_index · Index, amplify and purify the spatial library
  • spatial_QC_op · Inspect spatial library fragment sizes
Delegated endogenous plate continuation · Module plate_endogenous_module

Retained plate endogenous cDNA follows the separate IVT/transcriptome-library route rather than spatial PCR.

  • plate_IVT · Amplify endogenous plate material by IVT
  • plate_RNA_library_op · Construct the delegated plate transcriptome library
Droplet capture and source-qualified library continuation · Module droplet

Keeps the custom amplification/separation boundary qualified, and distinguishes guide endogenous-library chemistry, analytical aliquots and the yield-to-cycle control.

  • droplet_capture · Capture and copy molecules in 10X GEMs
  • droplet_recover · Break GEMs and purify first-strand products
  • droplet_amp_partition · Amplify and partition adapted droplet products
  • droplet_endogenous_recover · Recover endogenous cDNA for library construction
  • droplet_QC_aliquot · Take endogenous-cDNA QC aliquot
  • droplet_cDNA_measure · Measure cDNA and estimate carry-forward yield
  • droplet_library_aliquot_op · Allocate endogenous cDNA to the guide library route
  • droplet_fragment · Fragment, end-repair/A-tail and select endogenous cDNA
  • droplet_ligate · Ligate endogenous-library adapters and clean
  • droplet_index · Index, amplify and purify endogenous 10X library
  • droplet_library_QC_take · Take final endogenous-library QC aliquot
  • droplet_library_QC_measure · Inspect final endogenous library
Alternative MAT molecular construction · Module mat

Preserves simultaneous copying/marking, protected genomic digestion, dual-origin barcoding and separately prepared enriched/unenriched endogenous continuations.

  • mat_capture · Sort and lyse single cells for multiomics
  • mat_copy_mark · Copy RNA/PHO while marking accessible chromatin
  • mat_protect_digest · Strip chromatin, protect 5hmC and digest genomic DNA
  • mat_ligate_pool · Barcode genomic fragments and pool MAT wells
  • mat_partition · Separate spatial tags from endogenous MAT material
  • mat_IVT · Amplify endogenous MAT products by IVT
  • mat_allocate · Reserve enriched and unenriched analytical portions
  • mat_RNA_enrich · Enrich transcript-derived amplified RNA
  • mat_RNA_library_op · Continue enriched RNA to transcriptome library
  • mat_epigenome_library_op · Construct unenriched MAT epigenomic library
Sequencing distinct libraries · Module readout

Sequencing converts separate molecular libraries into their route-qualified read datasets without merging incompatible constructs.

  • sequence_spatial · Sequence spatial libraries
  • sequence_RNA · Sequence selected endogenous transcriptome library
  • sequence_epigenome · Sequence the MAT epigenomic library
Spatial decoding and optional reference estimator · Module spatial_analysis

Decodes cell/oligo identities and light-dose ratios; optional calibration and evaluation are data dependencies, not physical illumination feedback.

  • decode_spatial · Decode and deduplicate PHO/MPO reads
  • calculate_ratios · Calculate PHO cleavage-ratio measurements
  • infer_position · Interpret PHO ratios using the selected optical design
  • dose_reference · Construct optional known-dose reference regions
  • vote_dose · Assign optional multiple-PHO dose votes
  • evaluate_dose · Evaluate optional dose assignment
Transcriptomic and epigenomic analysis · Module endogenous_analysis

Applies distinct transcriptome pipelines and explicit genomic context rules while retaining cell-level cross-modal attribution.

  • map_plate_RNA · Count plate and MAT transcripts
  • map_droplet_RNA · Count droplet transcripts
  • analyze_RNA · Select and analyze transcriptomes
  • decode_epigenome · Call genomic marks and distinguish their origin
  • analyze_epigenome · Bin and attribute epigenomic profiles
Conditional bulk reference and genomic comparison · Module reference_comparison

Provides the independent material-to-data bulk reference required only by the declared within-sample regional-normalization mode, alongside optional external DNase annotations.

  • bulk_isolate · Isolate separate bulk reference gDNA
  • bulk_strip_mark · Strip chromatin and mark bulk reference GpCs
  • bulk_library · Prepare bulk-reference MspJI-seq library
  • sequence_bulk · Sequence the separate bulk-reference library
  • decode_bulk · Call bulk-reference detected sites
  • compare_regions · Perform optional referenced genomic comparisons
Cell-linked declared endpoint · Module joint_endpoint

Links already decoded cell-attributed optical and endogenous measurements at the declared assay endpoint.

  • integrate_readouts · Link optical and endogenous single-cell readouts
